fund.shortSummary: Capital support for small rural care providers adding telehealth equipment or clinic broadband capacity.
audience: Federally qualified clinic lookalikes in rural areas

goodFit: Applicant is a rural clinic or mobile health unit
Project improves telehealth or clinic connectivity
Clinic can attest to patient privacy controls
poorFit: Applicant sells software instead of delivering care
Project is only billing or back-office software

evaluationGuidance.reviewPriorities: Resolve hard-disqualifier checks before competitiveness signals: the applicant must deliver care, the funded site or mobile unit must be rural or frontier, the focus must be telehealth equipment or broadband/network capacity, and privacy attestation must be in place.
evaluationGuidance.borderlineHandling: For telehealth equipment, 199 annual patients misses the patient-volume criterion; do not round up. Broadband readiness requires a carrier quote or engineering plan, not a general intent to improve service. Local match below 5000 USD is advisory, not a hard failure.
evaluationGuidance.definitions: Care delivery provider means the organization serving patients and operating the asset. Broadband or network capacity includes connectivity hardware, installation, or carrier service upgrades; billing-only tools are back-office software.
evaluationGuidance.communicationEmphasis: Keep the tone operational and reassuring for small providers. Distinguish eligibility gaps from readiness gaps, and direct applicants to concrete fixes: apply through the care provider, narrow the site, or complete privacy controls.

progress.displayHint: Show answered questions over answered plus shortest remaining reachable questions from the current node.

questions.prompt: What type of organization is applying?
questions.helpText: Choose the organization that would own the funded equipment or broadband contract.

options.label: Independent rural clinic
options.helpText: A standalone primary or specialty care clinic that is not part of a hospital network and delivers direct patient care.

options.label: Mobile health unit
options.helpText: A vehicle-based care delivery unit that travels to patients in rural or frontier areas.

options.label: Hospital system
options.helpText: A multi-facility health system with at least one rural or frontier patient care site that would own the funded asset.

options.label: Software vendor
options.helpText: A company that develops or sells health IT software but does not itself deliver direct patient care.

questions.prompt: What type of county will the funded site primarily serve?
questions.helpText: Use the county classification of the patient care site or mobile unit home base.

options.label: Rural county
options.helpText: A county with a rural designation under USDA or HRSA classification; typically low population density outside metropolitan statistical areas.

options.label: Frontier county
options.helpText: A county with very low population density, typically six or fewer people per square mile, and limited health service infrastructure.

options.label: Urban county
options.helpText: A metropolitan or suburban county that does not meet rural or frontier classification under federal definitions.

questions.prompt: What is the primary project focus?
questions.helpText: Telehealth equipment, broadband upgrades, and billing software follow different readiness checks.

options.label: Telehealth exam equipment
options.helpText: Devices that enable clinical exams or consultations remotely, such as digital cameras, connected stethoscopes, or telehealth carts.

options.label: Broadband or network upgrade
options.helpText: Connectivity infrastructure such as fiber installation, router upgrades, or a new carrier service contract for the clinic or mobile unit.

options.label: Billing or back-office software
options.helpText: Software used primarily for claims processing, scheduling, or administrative operations rather than direct patient interaction.

questions.prompt: How many unique patients did the site serve last year?
questions.helpText: Use an estimate if the final annual report is not yet complete.

questions.prompt: What evidence do you have for the broadband upgrade?
questions.helpText: A carrier quote or engineering plan shows the project is ready to price and implement.

options.label: Carrier quote
options.helpText: A written cost estimate from a telecom or internet service provider specifying service scope, pricing, and delivery timeline.

options.label: Engineering plan
options.helpText: A technical design document identifying the infrastructure changes, equipment, and implementation steps required.

options.label: No plan yet
options.helpText: No formal document exists yet; the upgrade is at the idea or interest stage without a specific vendor or design.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of the billing or back-office software request?
questions.helpText: Record whether the request is tied to patient access or only administrative operations for the agent review.

options.label: Telehealth scheduling or access support
options.helpText: Software used to book and manage telehealth appointments or connect patients to remote clinical visits.

options.label: Claims or billing processing
options.helpText: Software used to submit insurance claims, check eligibility, or manage revenue cycle operations.

options.label: General administration
options.helpText: Software for back-office tasks such as HR, payroll, or internal operations not tied to patient access or clinical workflows.

questions.prompt: How much local matching support is committed?
questions.helpText: Include cash, equipment donations, waived installation costs, or documented in-kind technical labor.

questions.prompt: When could implementation begin after award notice?
questions.helpText: Use the first realistic date after procurement or carrier coordination can start.

questions.prompt: Can the applicant attest that patient privacy and security controls are in place for the funded use?
questions.helpText: This includes policies, access controls, and staff training appropriate for telehealth or network operations.

terminals.title: Confirm your rural clinic digital access answers
terminals.message: Review the complete answer summary. After confirmation, the agent will assess eligibility against the rural clinic digital access rules and explain any gaps.

eligibilityRules.criterion: The applicant must be a care delivery provider that will own or operate the funded equipment or broadband assets, not a software or equipment vendor.
eligibilityRules.remediation: Apply through the clinic, mobile health unit, or care delivery organization that will own and operate the funded assets; vendors may participate only as suppliers.

eligibilityRules.criterion: The funded site or mobile unit home base must primarily serve a rural or frontier county.
eligibilityRules.remediation: Limit the project to a rural or frontier patient care site, or document that the mobile unit is based in and primarily serves such a county.

eligibilityRules.criterion: The project must fund telehealth equipment or broadband/network upgrades rather than billing or general back-office software.
eligibilityRules.remediation: Replace billing or administrative software costs with eligible telehealth equipment, network hardware, installation, or broadband upgrade expenses.

eligibilityRules.criterion: For telehealth equipment projects, the funded site must serve at least 200 unique patients annually.
eligibilityRules.remediation: Delay applying until the site can document at least 200 unique patients annually, or partner with another eligible clinic to meet the service threshold.

eligibilityRules.criterion: For broadband projects, the applicant must have a carrier quote or engineering plan identifying scope, cost, and implementation approach.
eligibilityRules.remediation: Obtain a carrier quote or engineering plan that identifies scope, cost, and implementation approach before submitting the application.

eligibilityRules.criterion: The applicant must be able to attest that patient privacy and security controls are in place for the funded use.
eligibilityRules.remediation: Complete and document privacy policies, role-based access controls, and staff training before using grant-funded telehealth or network systems.

eligibilityRules.criterion: The application should document at least 5000 USD in committed local matching support.
eligibilityRules.remediation: Secure at least 5000 USD in committed cash, donated equipment, waived installation fees, or documented in-kind technical labor to make the application more competitive.
